question.text: Which of the following instruments can Indian companies issue to foreign investors under FDI norms?

answer.text: Equity shares, non-convertible debentures, and warrants
Equity shares, optionally convertible debentures, and preference shares
Equity shares, fully and mandatorily convertible debentures, fully and mandatorily convertible preference shares, and warrants

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 212-213 of the workbook list the FDI-norm instruments that Indian companies can issue as equity shares, fully and mandatorily convertible debentures, fully and mandatorily convertible preference shares and warrants, subject to pricing guidelines, valuation norms and reporting requirements under FEMA Regulations. The Trap: Non-convertible debentures fall outside the FDI list because they do not convert into equity; page 226 (review question) also treats optionally convertible shares as not being FDI-norm instruments. Page 218 supports ECB treatment for non-convertible/redeemable preference shares or debentures in the normal course. Note: The source-backed FDI instruments are the fully and mandatorily convertible instruments plus warrants; broader claims about all optionally convertible instruments being treated as ECB are not part of this answer.
